# Fire engine validation suite

`frontend/tests/fireValidation.test.ts` runs in `npm test`. `frontend/tests/fireValidationSlow.test.ts` skips itself unless `RUN_SLOW_TESTS` is set. It runs nightly (`.github/workflows/nightly-slow-tests.yml`) or locally with `npm run test:slow`.

The tolerances are Decision 5 of the realistic-fire roadmap:

- Upper-layer temperature rise within 20%.
- Interface height within 0.2 m or 15% of the ceiling, whichever is larger.
- Door mass flow within 25%.
- Time to flashover within 20%. Flashover is a 600 °C upper layer or 20 kW/m² on the floor.

A case outside its tolerance is an expected failure, listed under Known gaps below. Its test asserts two things: the case is still outside the tolerance, and the model still gives the recorded number within a pin. If a fix brings the case inside the tolerance, or a regression moves the number, the test fails. Then update this file.

The layer is compared with the measurement, not with a CFAST run. Measured rises are taken above the extract's first lower-layer temperature. The model's ambient is 293 K, so only rises are compared. Each value is a mean over the extract rows inside the case's window.

## Provenance

The measured layers are NIST's reduced layer files from [firemodels/exp](https://github.com/firemodels/exp) at commit `a9511fc4f56c3ae125d1d090e3be08e76959e856`. Each CSV here repeats its source, file and commit in its `#` header. The rows are unchanged; only whitespace was removed. The geometry, linings and fire curves in `cases.ts` are copied from the CFAST validation inputs in [firemodels/cfast](https://github.com/firemodels/cfast) at commit `b86959775ec32c5f3d95580cc0e3da2135da20ee`. Both repositories are NIST-developed, are not subject to US copyright, and are acknowledged here as the source.

| Extract                    | firemodels/exp file                         | CFAST input                          | Window                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `nbs-mv100a-fire-room.csv` | `NBS_Multi-Room/NBS_MV100A_Tree1_layer.csv` | `Validation/NBS/MV100A.in`           | 300–880 s                        |
| `nbs-mv100a-corridor.csv`  | `NBS_Multi-Room/NBS_MV100A_Tree4_layer.csv` | `Validation/NBS/MV100A.in`           | 300–880 s                        |
| `nist-nrc-be3-test03.csv`  | `NIST_NRC/NIST_NRC_Test_03_layer.csv`       | `Validation/NIST_NRC/NIST_NRC_T3.in` | 600–1200 s (nightly: 300–1379 s) |
| `vtt-be2-case1.csv`        | `VTT/BE2_Case_1_layer.csv`                  | `Validation/VTT/VTT_C1.in`           | 180–420 s                        |
| `vtt-be2-case2.csv`        | `VTT/BE2_Case_2_layer.csv`                  | `Validation/VTT/VTT_C2.in` (nightly) | 180–360 s                        |

Steckler uses the published values already in `twoZone.test.ts`: Johansson and van Hees (IAFSS 2014, Table 3) for the interface and the rise, and NBSIR 82-2520 for the full-door centre run (outflow 0.571 kg/s, inflow 0.554 kg/s, neutral plane 1.027 m).

These parts of the setup differ from the tests:

- **Vents.** Single-room cases vent to ambient. The NBS fire room opens into the entry in `MV100A.in` (1.02 m × 1.03 m × 2.00 m, Marinite walls and ceiling, gypsum floor, a 0.81 m × 1.6 m door each way). The fire-room door uses that entry's layer as the other side of CFAST Eq. 4.1, and the leaving gas is the entry's door jet. The entry's other door opens to ambient in `runNbsFireRoom`. A production door between two indoor rooms sets `Vent.outside` from the other room's layer at the previous step. A door to the outdoors, and a neighbour that has no layer yet, stays ambient. The jet still carries the hot gas, the unburned fuel, and the spill plume. A room that deposits that jet leaves the matching upper-layer inflow out of the orifice, and the interface takes jet volume only for the part that orifice did not balance, so the stream is counted once in mass and in volume. Outflow from below the interface is booked in every room. A room with its own fire does not deposit the carrier; the orifice is the return. Extending the fire-room fixture through the corridor, with each indoor door seeing the neighbour and the jets lagged one step the way the engine lags them, leaves the fire room at 0.86 m and 200 K over 300–880 s, inside both bands. The entry is 1.00 m and 148 K. The corridor there is 1.18 m and 33 K: the interface is inside ±0.37 m of 1.32 m and the rise is not. That rise is the model limit of the receiving corridor. The fire-room pin stays the entry. The corridor comparison itself runs on the stud plan (FV-4).
- **The target-room door.** The corridor's 0.79 m × 2.04 m door to the target-room entry is left out. In MV100A it is shut for the whole test (CFAST `WallVent_4` and `WallVent_5` have open fraction F = 0 at all times; the title is "No Target Room").
- **Burner position.** The NBS burner stands 0.1 m from a wall. The plume stays free. CFAST's technical reference does not apply a wall correction: McGrattan, NIST TN 1984, found no significant effect of a wall on entrainment. The VTT pan stands 1 m above the floor (the CFAST `HEIGHT`), and Heskestad's z is measured from the pan. Entraining from the floor instead puts Case 1 at 3.76 m and 34.7 K. From the pan it is 4.65 m and 36.0 K.
- **VTT geometry.** The hall's cross-section is the `CROSS_SECT` rows of `VTT_C1.in` and `VTT_C2.in`: 372.6 m² from the floor to the 12 m eaves, a pyramid to 51.3 m² at 17.1 m, and 51.3 m² up to the 19 m monitor (CFAST user's guide §4.4). The steel stays the hall's real surface. Carrying the floor area up to the ridge was 4.65 m and 36.0 K on Case 1, and 4.02 m and 57.2 K on Case 2.
- **VTT steel.** The shell is 1 mm and stores about 3.3 kJ/m²K. Against the two films that is on the order of two minutes, and both windows open while the shell is still warming. The sheet is one temperature, ρ c δ dT/dt, with the inside film and χQ/A warming it and CFAST's exterior film cooling the back. A heat-free sheet, the same films with no capacity, was 42.3 K and 67.2 K. A board keeps k/δ to ambient. The Biot gate that chooses a sheet is this engine's choice: CFAST applies the exterior film to every wall. The gate uses 4σT³ at ambient, the weakest film, so it is permissive. 6 mm glass crosses it. A glass-walled room is disclosed in Decision 10. The sheet temperature is stored by wall id. A sheet no layer is stepping cools toward ambient through both films. A partition two layers share is integrated once, from both gases. The fallout model keeps its own pane temperature: it is the local point source and it freezes at the crack, while the sheet is the wall-average χQ/A the gas is charged. One temperature would either drop that crack or count the flame's radiation twice. Glass is taken as opaque: short-wave radiation a real pane would transmit outdoors is absorbed with χQ/A, and that transmission is a known gap.

## Known gaps

### FV-1

**Steckler doorway flow.** The coupled steady outflow is 0.382 kg/s against the measured 0.571 kg/s, which is −33%. The 25% band runs from 0.428 to 0.714 kg/s. The test pins the outflow at 0.392 ± 0.03 kg/s. That steady root holds the lower gas at ambient. It is an interface of 1.18 m and a rise of 105 K, and a neutral plane of 1.23 m against the measured 1.027 m. That plane is 0.20 m high. Decision 5 has no band for the neutral plane, so the pass borrows the interface height band, ±0.32 m. The regression pin is 1.229 ± 0.02 m. The 600 s integration, which lets the lower layer warm, is the interface and the rise in the table. The rise of that integration is FV-6. Roadmap: Decision 7, "Known gap: the Steckler doorway flow".

The three numbers are one mass-flow deficit. Heskestad at the measured 0.985 m entrains 0.301 kg/s. The orifice held at that height is 0.528 kg/s at the model's 122 K rise for that height. The neutral plane on that hold is 1.10 m. The flow is inside 25% of 0.571 kg/s, and the plane is within 0.08 m of 1.027 m. The coupled root is the height where the plume and the door are equal, at 0.382 kg/s and 1.18 m. The 600 s layer is hotter than that steady root; its rise is FV-6.

Inflow between the interface and the neutral plane is 0.010 kg/s at the coupled root and 0.037 kg/s at 0.985 m. That is the band a slice beside the upper layer would join (CFAST TN 1889v1 Fig. 4.1). It leaves the door about 0.2 kg/s short. McCaffrey's three-region plume, coupled the same way, is about 0.42 kg/s. The inverse door jet (CFAST Eq. 4.7, Cm = 0.44) entrains about 0.005 kg/s at this interface and moves the outflow from 0.385 kg/s to 0.381 kg/s. NBSIR 83-2801 gives opening coefficients of about 0.68 in and 0.73 out. This orifice uses CFAST's 0.7. The held-interface flow is already inside 25%, so the coefficient is not the remaining third.

NBSIR 82-2520 measured the entrainment directly. Fires near a wall agree with a free plume. For a corner the report notes some interference by the walls. Fires away from the walls, except the smallest openings, entrain two to three times a free plume, because the doorway inflow tilts the plume the way a cross wind does. Quintiere, Rinkinen and Jones (Combustion Science and Technology 26, 1981, 193–201) recover a tilted plume by using an entrainment length Z/sin θ, with θ the angle from the horizontal. Steckler did not measure θ on these runs. A factor chosen so this centre burner hits 0.571 kg/s would be a fit to one row, and the same report's wall fires match the free plume. The plume stays Heskestad. The gap stays this pin.

### FV-2

**The 1 MW flashover latch.** `FLASHOVER_ROOM_KW` lights every fuelled stud in a room once the burning fuel sums to 1000 kW. In the NUREG room that is below all three correlations: Thomas 1625 kW, Babrauskas 1909 kW and MQH 2366 kW. The layer alone reaches the flashover definition at 2078 kW, which is inside the band. Pinned at 1000 kW. Roadmap: Decision 8, where the 1 MW latch still ignites the fuel and is described as a stand-in.

### FV-4

**Corridor rise from a door jet.** The upper-layer gas that leaves a vent is deposited in the next room: mass at the source temperature, so the enthalpy is m cp (T_jet − T). A room that takes the jet already has that stream in the orifice, so jet volume moves the interface only for the part the orifice did not balance. Subtracting the whole jet volume as well counts that volume twice. Outflow from below the interface is booked in every room. A room with no fire of its own can hold a layer. A room that already has a fire keeps its own vent balance and does not take a second copy of the neighbour's jet.

The measured corridor layer is 1.32 m with an 80.2 K rise. On the engine plan the interface is 0.947 m, −28%, 7 mm outside ±0.37 m, and the rise is 39.5 K, −51%, outside 20%. The interface is pinned at 0.947 ± 0.01 m and the rise at 39.5 ± 1 K. The split had put the interface at 0.955 m, inside the band. Booking the lower layer from the root's flows moved it back outside by 7 mm. Before the layer split the same plan was 0.930 m and 33.2 K. Roadmap: "What to reproduce", the two-room case.

The rise gap is what the receiving corridor does with the jet. In the test geometry the corridor has its Marinite walls, the entry is its own room, the fire room is 200 K and the entry is 148 K, and the corridor rise is still 33 K against 80.2 K. That miss stays with the linings the test used, so it is a model limit. The stud plan's concrete is a separate measurement. The entry is not its own room there: a diagonal stud link meets the end of the corridor-entry wall, so the entry stud is part of the corridor and the jet enters one 45 m² room (`c0`–`c3` and `entry`). The jet leaves the plan's fire room at about a 102 K rise over 300–880 s (the interface there is 0.94 m). The test's fire room, stopped at the entry, is 246 K. While the corridor door saw ambient, that plan fire room was 1.08 m and 88.6 K, an adiabatic corridor reached about 90 K, and concrete took 61% of the jet enthalpy (27.2 MJ of 44.9 MJ over 0–880 s), leaving a 33.4 K mean. That earlier coupled plan was 33.2 K, the same band as the Marinite corridor. The split lifts the stud-plan rise to 39.5 K.

In the test geometry the corridor interface is 1.18 m, inside ±0.37 m of 1.32 m. On the stud plan the split put it at 0.955 m, inside the band, and booking the root's flows left it at 0.947 m, 7 mm outside. Before the split it was 0.930 m. The plan still merges the entry into the corridor, uses 2.0 m door heads, and stands concrete in for ceramic fibre and Marinite.

The test runs `nbsPlan.ts` through `SpatialEffectsEngine`: the fire room, entry and corridor on the stud grid, joined by the two 0.81 m doors, with the corridor's 0.76 m outside door as the building exit and a 110 kW pool stud in the fire room. The plan keeps the test's topology, not its dimensions:

- The studs are whole 9 m² cells: the fire room one, the entry one, the corridor four. The engine then merges the entry into the corridor.
- There is one 2.44 m storey.
- The linings are concrete.
- Each door has a 2.0 m head.
- The burner's radiative fraction is 0.35.

In the same plan the fire room is 0.94 m with a 102 K rise. Over 300–880 s the corridor has a layer in 59 of 59 samples, at 0.947 m and 39.5 K. The mean corridor extinction is 0.354 ± 0.02 /m.

**The arrival door sees the fire room, and the jet's volume is booked once.** While that door solved against ambient, the interface was 1.13 m. About 23% of the jet enthalpy (10.4 MJ of 44.9 MJ) flowed back out through the door it arrived by, and the corridor let out 614 kg after receiving 519 kg. The fire room discards that return jet, because a room with its own fire does not take the carrier. Removing that ambient relief is right. Counting the jet's volume again, after the orifice had already included the same stream, dropped the interface to 0.274 m and left the lower-layer budget short by about 420 kg, which is the jet. With lower-layer outflow booked and jet volume taken only for the unmatched part, the budget closes. The split moved the interface from 0.930 m to 0.955 m. Booking the root's flows leaves it at 0.947 m. The jet mass deposited still matches the upper-layer inflow the orifice leaves out, so the stream is not counted twice in mass or in volume. The rise stayed near 33 K in the Marinite corridor on that earlier measurement, so the remaining gap is the receiving room. The stud plan is still 0.37 m below 1.32 m: door heads of 2.0 m, the entry merged into the corridor, and concrete standing in for the test's linings. Every room books outflow from below its interface. A burning room whose door faces a hot neighbour can send about half of its outflow out of the lower layer, and the height change includes that flow. The Harbour mall has its own outdoor doors; its interface is the scene golden, not this corridor.

**Head height is a switch.** While the interface is above 1.7 m the head reads the lower layer. For a jet-formed layer that is the soot already there at activation, decaying at the column leak (0.002/s), not the layer. When the interface crosses 1.7 m the stud is set to the layer's extinction, capped at the smoke scale (6.1 /m). In the Harbour mall the layer is already on the order of 100 /m by the crossing near T+500, so the reading steps to the cap in one frame. A sharp interface into a layer that thick is opaque over a few centimetres. A blend width would be an assumed thickness this model does not have. Fire-driven layers still clear the column when they form: they form within seconds, before that soot is there.

### FV-6

**Steckler rise after the layer split.** At 600 s the interface is 1.15 m, inside ±0.32 m of 0.985 m, and the rise is 121 K against 98.2 K, +23%, 3 K outside ±20%. The pin is 121 ± 1 K. The lower layer is 19 K above ambient. The plume entrains that air, and the floor, cooled by the lower gas, conducts about 1 kW less than the one-gas film did. Before the split the same 600 s was 1.18 m and 113 K, inside the band. The steady balance still holds the lower gas at ambient and is 1.18 m and 105 K, which would pass; the integration is the row. No emissivity or door coefficient was moved to recover the 3 K. Charging the floor's whole film to the lower gas, instead of only its convection, took the rise to 131 K and pushed BE#3 outside its band. Roadmap: Decision 7.

## Closed

**FV-3, the NBS fire room.** A door straight to ambient gave 183 K against 242 K, with the interface at 0.986 m. χ = 0 moved the rise to 181 K. An adiabatic lining reached the 1500 K ceiling. Gas radiation set to zero reached 195 K and took BE#3 from 189 K to 233 K. A free plume at 0.7 of Heskestad reached 215 K. The door opens into the entry, and that entry on Eq. 4.1 puts the window at 0.663 m and 246 K. Both are inside the band. Production doors between rooms now set the same neighbour gauge; a door to the outdoors stays ambient. Putting the corridor on the entry's far door, with the engine's one-step jet lag, left the fire room at 0.86 m and 200 K before the layer split, still inside the band, and the corridor at 1.18 m and 33 K. The corridor rise is outside 20% with the test's own Marinite, so that gap is the receiving corridor and the pin stays the entry.

**FV-5, the VTT hall.** The box of floor area up to the ridge was 4.65 m and 36.0 K, and on the nightly Case 2 it was 4.02 m and 57.2 K. The cross-section in the geometry note puts Case 1 at 4.12 m and 45.0 K (−20% and −7%) and Case 2 at 3.26 m and 71.4 K (−29% and −8%). Both pass. The steel still stores ρ c δ. A heat-free sheet on the old box was 42.3 K and 67.2 K; that pass was the missing capacity, and the coldness that remained was the extra volume above the eaves. The two cases still start from ambient. A temperature left on the shared sheet is not the case.

## FDS

An offline FDS 6.11.2 comparison of a two-room box and a Harbour shop and mall is in `fds/README.md`. It is a regime check, not a test, and the device files are not in git.

The production Harbour shop leaves a 35 kg total-mass residual once the interface is on the 0.05 m floor clamp. On those steps the plume may take only the lower inflow plus the mass still above the floor. The rest of the Heskestad draw is upper gas recirculating, and it moves no mass. Steps that are already on the floor draw 374 kg of plume against 375 kg of inflow, and their residual is 14 kg. The other 21 kg arrives with the descent and is the unclipped volume of the shortfalls that are not the plume. Above the clamp the lower-layer budget closes within 5 kg. The previous expansion head measured 572 kg on the same clamp, the exchange booking measured 566 kg, and booking the root's flows without this cap left 1753 kg. The rate is not clipped to hide the residual.

The jet-fed mall still closes in total and not per layer. Over the 224 s it spends above the floor, the lower layer is 246 kg below the flows booked to it, and the room total against the vents closes within 0.5 kg. The unmatched part of the jet takes lower-layer volume that no vent is booked to carry. That is the displacement the deposited-jet test keeps, and this change does not rewrite it.
